allowedSourceMaterial.overview: The fastest man on four wheels, Ricky Bobby, is one of the greatest drivers in NASCAR history. A big, hairy American winning machine, Ricky has everything a dimwitted daredevil could want, a luxurious mansion, a smokin' hot wife, and all the fast food he can eat. But Ricky's turbo-charged lifestyle hits an unexpected speed bump when he's bested by flamboyant Euro-idiot Jean Girard and reduced to a fear-ridden wreck.

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: When an arrogant European challenger shatters Ricky Bobby's winning streak, will the fallen champion conquer his terror and reclaim the track?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: NASCAR sensation Ricky Bobby enjoys fame, wealth, and endless victories until flamboyant rival Jean Girard challenges his dominance, sending the daredevil driver spiraling into a paralyzing crisis of confidence.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Fast, raucous, and completely lighthearted. An easy-watching racing farce built for big laughs with friends.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Adam McKay directs a fast, wildly energetic sports comedy loaded with outsized rivalries and unhinged humor, making it an effortless crowd-pleaser for a fun group watch.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: Two items sit near the tolerance line. 'Arrogant' in curiosityHook replaces the source's 'flamboyant' with a different trait attribute for Jean Girard. I read it as characterization shorthand in the same class as 'ruthless' for 'murderous', since it does not change his role or the plot. 'Shatters Ricky Bobby's winning streak' implies a specific unbroken run, where the overview says only that he was 'bested', and 'reclaim the track' hints at a comeback goal. The second is posed as a question and asserts no outcome. A stricter adjudicator could ask for 'flamboyant' to be restored and 'streak' softened, in which case they would be MINOR characterization and concretization issues.
